questions.q: The latency budget for a tracking loop is set by:
options: The median of the first 10 runs
questions.explain: One slow frame in the middle of a maneuver is a lost target.

questions.q: The first quantization step on a GPU, with almost no loss of accuracy:
questions.explain: FP16 usually costs nothing in accuracy.

questions.q: PTQ was calibrated on daytime frames only. The expected consequence:
options: Accuracy rises at night because of the noise
questions.explain: Activation ranges are different in other conditions.

questions.q: Why is the held-out set split by flight and not by frame?
options: It is faster to label and train that way
questions.explain: Near-identical frames leak between train and test.

questions.q: After 20 minutes of operation p99 doubled. The most likely cause:
options: A memory leak in the model weights
questions.explain: Profile inside the enclosure, and for a long time.

questions.q: A model layer that the accelerator does not support:
questions.explain: It runs on the CPU and can eat the whole gain; the engine profiler shows it right away.

questions.q: In a search for people, the detector threshold should reasonably move toward:
questions.explain: The operator will check the false alarms.

questions.q: What must be written to the log of every flight with ML on board?
questions.explain: Without the version, incident analysis is impossible.

questions.q: The tracking loop budget is 80 ms. The detector profile on board:
questions.fragment: n=300 mean=41.2 p50=33.8 p95=96.4 p99=211.7 max=402.3 budget_ms=80 ok=False over_budget_frac=0.07
options: The mean fits, but the tail (p95/p99) does not: 7 % of the frames exceed the budget, find the source
over_budget_frac = 0.07 is perf_counter timer error, not real slow frames
p50 = 34 ms means the model is underloaded and can be replaced with a heavier one
All is fine: the budget is checked against the mean, and 41 ms is less than 80
questions.explain: A loop budget is checked against p99: slow frames in the middle of a maneuver lose the target.
